pr_title: Retrieve the source for objects and arrays within arrays in a separate parsing phase
pr_body:
In synthetic source, storing array elements to `_ignored_source` may hide other, regular elements from showing up during source synthesizing. This is due to contents from `_ignored_source` taking precedence over matching fields from regular source loading. 

To avoid this, arrays are pre-emptively tracked and marked for source storing, if any of their elements needs to store its source. A second doc parsing phase is introduced that checks for fields missing values and records their source, while skipping objects and arrays that don't contain any such fields.

Fixes #112374
pr_comments: Hi @kkrik-es, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> I see that currently we store some things in first phase and some things in second phase. I think it would be cleaner to do everything in second phase and only record field names in first phase. I haven't thought about implications of this though.
> 
> Overall looks great.

I'm mostly worried about performance - the second pass may be slow as it checks all field names against a hash map.. I was actually thinking of restricting its use to nested arrays - the case where the bug appears. Lemme use rally to ballpark the impact to indexing performance.

I am not sure how to fix this. Merging ignored source with native synthetic source is not correct since we would see first value twice. Maybe we can remove separate code path for arrays and always store objects in ignored source if `store_array_source` is true, no matter if they are inside arrays.

For `dynamic: runtime` case we should be able to just remove piece of logic that handles arrays, store individual values in ignored source and rely on recently introduced merging of ignored source values. It would work for objects too (since we parse them in the same order as they are in the document) with a drawback of unnecessarily storing individual objects. 

I can imagine some clever solution that preserves object source in ignored source and then looks if there are more objects being parsed. If that is true, all good, if not, we remove the entry from ignored source since we should be good with native impl.
